pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind feature

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Add test to cover network policies when both Ingress and Egress are specified

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #87893

**Special notes for your reviewer**:
I found that running e2e tests on local computer might be challenging for beginners, I used combination of https://github.com/kubernetes/community/blob/master/contributors/devel/sig-testing/e2e-tests.md https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kind/issues/1181#issuecomment-567001724 and custom CNI plugin (Calico) installed in kind.

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

issue_context.title: Ingress,Egress tests for NetworkPolicys
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please only use this template for submitting enhancement requests -->

**What would you like to be added**:

We are missing a test which specifies Ingress,Egress (both) for network policys (in network_policy.go).

**Why is this needed**:

So that our network policy test coverage matches the semantics of what is commented and supported in the API.

review_comments: Is it possible to add helper func to create/generate the needed network policy? It isn't too easy to parse this and having a big chunk of struct specification makes codes less readable :)

Yeah, I know.

There is an issue here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/88375#issuecomment-589331799 and @jayunit100 works on KEP I believe.

I'm not familiar with these tests so please bear with me, but this is interesting 🤔 
 how do the tests know that the failure to connect is caused by the ingress or the egress?
`default-deny-all` and `default-deny-ingress` have the same behavior but I can't see how do we exercise each policy
Thank you! You're totally right. this deny-all test should be more complex. I've updated PR, added pod in another namespace and check is it reachable after policy applied.
Wouldn't this collide with the other test case (when running in parallel) if we append the same suffix (the base namespace is the same)?
it wouldn’t, namespaces has unique suffix

Example from log
```
STEP: Creating a server pod server in namespace network-policy-2306
STEP: Creating a server pod pod-b in namespace network-policy-b-6489
```

There is no need to cleanup namespace, it will be cleaned up automatically when step is finished. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L485 

Example from log:
```
STEP: Destroying namespace "network-policy-2306" for this suite.
STEP: Destroying namespace "network-policy-b-6489" for this suite.
```
Would this namespace be cleaned up?
Yes, it will be cleaned up, covered here https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/test/e2e/framework/framework.go#L485
